transcript: Most addiction, most compulsive behavior is not cured by force, but by absence. A period of abstinence 30 to 60 days is often enough to restore the nervous system. To someone trapped in craving, that sounds unbearable, like punishment, like loss, but it is in fact medicine. I speak often with people who live on stimulation, work, deadlines, pressure, caffeine, medication, achievement, always pushing forward. Many come from technology or finance. They ask, why am I burned out? Because for years they have overstimulated the same reward circuits. They have lived in constant acceleration. The body responds eventually by shutting down feeling. When stimulation is removed, the first days feel empty, then a little less empty, then neutral. And only after neutrality can genuine vitality return. At that point, and only then, can stimulation be reintroduced wisely. Some medicines have a true place. Some people need them, but many are not deficient. They are exhausted. They have fallen into a dopamine trough, seeking relief in more noise, more effort, more urgency. When what is needed is patience. Wait, rest, travel, step away, learn to receive reward from smaller things. This is why animals teach us so much. A dog does not need access to feel alive. If this feels dull to you, heavy, uncomfortable, it is often a sign that the nervous system has forgotten how to be still.
